dataset.name: PARSEC
rationale: PARSEC is a classic benchmark suite for chip-multiprocessor and shared-memory studies.
The suite spans working set size, locality, sharing, synchronization, and off-chip traffic diversity.
It is a better first real-workload target than Redis/RocksDB/YCSB or SPEC CPU for the current QMAP trace-driven pipeline.

download_candidates.note: Verify availability from the Linux trace-collection host before Stage 2.
Fallback only if the original project site is unavailable.
Fallback for modern Linux builds; record any patch delta if used.

notes: Use Linux, WSL2, or a server for PARSEC build and tracing.
Keep raw PARSEC source, input archives, and full traces out of git unless a tiny sample is explicitly needed.
After capture, run chronological 80/10/10 split before JSONL generation.

selected_workloads.name: blackscholes
selected_workloads.why_selected: Provides a comparatively stable, compute-heavy baseline so QMAP can be checked against a workload where memory behavior should be less pathological.
selected_workloads.expected_signal: Moderate locality and comparatively limited write pressure; useful as a sanity baseline.

selected_workloads.name: canneal
selected_workloads.why_selected: Often used in memory-system studies and expected to stress locality and reuse behavior more than blackscholes.
selected_workloads.expected_signal: Irregular page reuse and nontrivial working-set pressure; useful for testing whether QMAP beats simple recency.

selected_workloads.name: streamcluster
selected_workloads.why_selected: Covers streaming/cluster-style behavior where reuse distance and working set shape may differ from synthetic hotset traces.
selected_workloads.expected_signal: Potentially weaker temporal reuse and larger working set; useful for defining QMAP's boundary conditions.

selected_workloads.name: dedup
selected_workloads.why_selected: Data deduplication pipeline can expose memory traffic from chunking, hashing, compression, and output handling.
selected_workloads.expected_signal: More useful than a purely compute-heavy workload for observing NVM writes and migration cost interactions.

fallback_workloads.name: ferret
fallback_workloads.why_fallback: Use if dedup build, dependencies, or trace capture are unstable. Ferret adds recognition/search-style behavior and is still useful for locality and sharing diversity.

stage1_decision.next_phase: Stage 2 should build PARSEC on Linux/WSL/server, capture PC/Address/RW traces, and write raw CSV files to dataset/raw_traces.
